chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: Boxing the newsboys in Indianapolis
summary: As the only Negro paper boy, he was made to box another boy and earned respect.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: During the time I was in Indianapolis when I was selling papers like the Indianapolis Star and the baseball extras, I used to have to go to the newspaper office to get my papers. So I'd get to the paper office to get my papers, quite a few of the boys -- me being the only negro boy seemed like was there picking up papers -- thought they'd want to have a little fisticuff with me. So they picked up the best one they thought could fight me and they got some gloves and put the gloves on us and everything, but I don't want to, I just had hurt my thumb sliding down a pole and got cut on the barbed wire fence and tore my thumb wide open. However, they didn't pay no attention they wanted me to put on these gloves and fight this boy and I had to do it. So I did. So we boxed and we boxed until they found out I was no slouch, you know. 'Cause I could fight a
while, you know, which I loved and I loved to fight, how I loved that. But I hate to get into an argument, 'cause I know he's going to make a fight out of it.
